story: Kessler (prop, firm capital; down ~400k this quarter, pay tied to book P&L) stacks five 25 ETH bids behind the touch (normal size ~3), price lifts ~7bp, sells 40 ETH, cancels the bids. Two prior layering alerts.
Same pattern on BTC later the same day.
Ortiz sold 200 calls to a client (short 60 delta), pulled her offers and bought 60 ETH to hedge.

Becker runs the firm's NOVA market-making agreement, which pays only if 30-day volume hits a KPI; the issuer warns renewal is at risk. He crosses 150k NOVA six times between LP-NOVA and AFF-0731, an account his family LLC owns that he never declared. Volume without change in ownership.
Brandt takes Calder's 300 ETH buy, buys 20 ETH in his personal account 25s later with no pre-clearance, works the client order, then sells his personal ETH into the move.
Lind's TWAP children overlap Westbrook's order, but ALGO-0917 was created and approved hours earlier.
Client-instructed cross between two Calder funds (same manager, different beneficial owners), at mid, documented.

Haddad (market maker) books a small call sale as cover: it leaves him short ~3 ETH of delta, so a hedge means BUYING ~3 ETH. Instead he stacks ~107 ETH of bids (his normal size ~4), lifts the price, SELLS ~31 ETH and cancels. The 'hedge' story doesn't match the size or the direction.

Okafor stacks ~1,580 SOL of offers (normal size ~25), pushes the price down, buys ~414 SOL, cancels. Then posts a message aimed at the AI reviewer. He is a prop trader with no clients, and no approval exists anywhere. The attempt to steer the review is itself a red flag.
